subject: Post-renewal usage spike & settlement plan
messages:
From: Elena Moretti <elena@corvus-analytics.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Corvus Analytics Finance <billing@corvus-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected post-renewal usage spike — need reconciliation

Hi Naomi,

We closed the renewal with Redwood on Aug 15 and immediately saw a usage bump the week after as we shipped a new recommendation feature. Our finance team is showing a significant retroactive usage charge for the July–August period that wasn't anticipated in the renewal forecast.

Can you help reconcile what triggered the spike and work with us on a settlement path? Specifically:
- We need a line-item breakdown of July and August usage tied to the model variants and regions.
- If there are one-time or billing errors, we'd like to understand any credits/reductions you can offer.
- We need an updated invoice or credit memo for our procurement team to process before Sep 15.

Attaching the preliminary bill we received (billing@ attached it). Can you confirm receipt and next steps?

Thanks,
Elena Moretti
Head of Product, Corvus Analytics
elena@corvus-analytics.com

--
Attachment: corvus-invoice-JulAug2026.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moretti <elena@corvus-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-renewal usage spike — need reconciliation

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and for forwarding the invoice. I've looped Ben from our billing team and Markus for visibility.

Quick plan:
1) Ben will pull the July/Aug usage breakdown by model and region and share a short spreadsheet (we'll flag any anomalous runs).
2) We'll validate whether usage lines map to the renewed SKUs or to any legacy meter that should not have been billed.
3) If there's a billing mistake or obvious one-time overage, we'll propose an adjustment + a one-time credit. If usage is valid but unexpected, we'll propose a remediation: a one-time credit + a capacity amendment for Q4 and a clearer forecast cadence.

Can you confirm the procurement contact who needs the adjusted invoice? Also, any internal PO/reference we should put on the credit memo?

I'll aim to get the first-pass analysis to you by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Elena Moretti <elena@corvus-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected post-renewal usage spike — need reconciliation

Naomi / Elena — I pulled the usage logs and ran a reconciliation against the renewal SKU mapping. Summary below (see attached workbook for line-by-line):

Summary findings:
- Total additional billed tokens (Jul1–Aug31): 1,125,400 tokens.
- 78% of the excess maps to calls routed to the rwd-large-v2 variant in us-west-2 after Aug 16.
- A small percentage (~3%) are agent-test keys we filtered out; those are billable but should have been under the dev account.

Proposed settlement:
- Offer a one-time credit of $3,200 to offset the unexpected charge; this reflects 40% of the July incremental usage and a goodwill adjustment for onboarding friction.
- Issue an adjusted invoice (credit memo) replacing the original one-time overage line with the net amount.
- Recommend a short-term capacity amendment: add +20% committed capacity for Q4 at the same unit pricing (to avoid another surprise while Corvus stabilizes traffic).

I've attached: corvus-usage-analysis-Jul-Aug2026.xlsx with the raw counts and a redline proposal for the invoice.

If accepted, I'll prepare the credit memo and updated invoice PDF for your procurement team.

Ben Carter
Billing Manager | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: corvus-usage-analysis-Jul-Aug2026.xlsx (Excel, 12 sheets)

- Put the Q4 committed capacity amendment in draft (simple amendment, term Oct 1–Dec 31, 2026) and route to Legal for a fast-sign.

Naomi, loop in our solutions engineer if Corvus needs help pinning the model routing to avoid repeated spikes.

-Markus

Subject: Re: Unexpected post-renewal usage spike — settlement & next steps

Hi Elena — thanks for your patience. Per the analysis and internal approvals, please find the settlement details below and next steps for procurement:

What we found:
• Incremental usage July–August tied primarily to rwd-large-v2 in us-west-2 after Aug 16.
• No evidence of a billing-system error; the charges reflect actual calls but we agree the spike arrived immediately post-renewal and disrupted your forecast.

What Redwood will do (agreed):
1) Apply a one-time credit of $3,200 against your overage line.
2) Issue adjusted invoice: Redwood Invoice ADJ-789 (attached). This replaces the overage line with the net amount and includes the credit memo language: "Goodwill adjustment related to post-renewal routing and onboarding noise."
3) Draft a short Q4 capacity amendment (+20% committed tokens) at current unit pricing; we will route the draft to your procurement/legal for signature.

Attachments: redwood-invoice-ADJ-789.pdf, signed-amendment-corvus.pdf (draft signed after internal approval — please treat as preliminary; final legal will produce official doc).

Procurement details: please confirm the PO number or reference we should include on the credit memo and the email address to send the final PDF for payment processing. If you need a different billing contact, let me know and we'll update.

If all looks good, I'll log the credit and queue the invoice for your accounts payable.

Best regards,
